editorial.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. Oct 6-20 papers cover a speculative-decoding attack surface, knowledge-graph-guided legal and secure-code work, sycophancy, and code-translation hallucinations.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 22 adds two arXiv papers: spectral smoothing/spiking interventions that shift LLM capability profiles, and an empirical benchmark of recent LLMs on knowledge-graph-to-text generation; neither extends earlier items.
editorial.why_it_matters: Each paper names a distinct failure or evaluation surface: draft-model attacks, sycophancy, hallucinated translated code, search-state blindness, weight-spectrum side effects. Treat them as separate checks, not one trend.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not cite these papers as corroborating each other; add a hallucination check on LLM-translated code, and wait for independent evals before adopting the search-state RL or spectral-editing methods.

open_questions: Does the speculative-decoding defense add measurable latency over unprotected drafting?
Do the code-translation mitigations hold on languages outside the paper's test set?
Does self-assessment RL improve search-agent accuracy on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does independent replication confirm the spectral-intervention capability shifts on other model families?
